judge_panel.reason: The paper provides no attention-map visualizations to empirically validate that the cross-attention in GL correctly establishes image-to-voxel correspondences for scene inputs; Appendix A.1 only describes the procedural choice of heads without any diagnostic figure showing alignment quality.

The method relies on the premise that "the flow transformer-based model GL within the TRELLIS framework learns to establish correspondences between image regions and 3D voxels" and that this "key insight enables us" to do 2D-to-3D lifting. Yet the paper only describes the attention extraction textually — e.g., "averaging ... head 0, 4, and 12" in Appendix A.1 — and provides no attention-map visualization or diagnostic figure supporting this premise on the paper’s examples.

The paper heavily relies on the cross-attention maps for hierarchical 2D-to-3D segmentation, but nowhere in the main text or appendix are visualisations of these attention maps provided to empirically validate their alignment quality.
